subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Compression in the Cloud
description: A short lesson to help you apply Data Compression in the Cloud.

hook.text: A company stores 100 TB of logs. Compression shrinks that to 10 TB. Storage cost drops 90% instantly.

buildup.text: Compression reduces data size for storage and transfer. Algorithms like gzip, zstd, and Snappy trade CPU for space.

discovery.text: Columnar formats like Parquet and ORC compress data 10x better than raw CSV or JSON for analytical workloads.

twist.text: Compression saves storage costs but increases compute costs. Decompressing data on every read takes CPU time.

climax.text: The right compression format depends on whether you optimize for storage cost, query speed, or transfer time.

punchline.text: Compress to save storage. Decompress to use data. Balance both.

quiz.question: What is the trade-off of data compression?
options: It saves storage costs but increases CPU usage when data needs to be read
Compressed data cannot be queried or searched
Compression only works on text files, not binary data

details.summary: Data compression reduces storage costs and transfer times in the cloud. Columnar formats like Parquet compress analytical data by 80 percent or more. Choosing the right compression algorithm balances size reduction against CPU cost for compression and decompression.
details.whyItMatters: At cloud scale, compression savings compound. Reducing data size by 80 percent cuts storage costs, speeds up queries, and reduces network transfer time and egress charges.
takeaways: Columnar formats like Parquet compress analytical data dramatically
Compression reduces storage, transfer, and query scan costs
Algorithm choice trades compression ratio against CPU cost

faq.question: What compression algorithms are common in the cloud?
faq.answer: Gzip offers good compression ratios for general use. Snappy and LZ4 provide fast compression and decompression for real-time workloads. Zstandard balances both. Columnar formats like Parquet use dictionary and run-length encoding for additional savings.

faq.question: Does compression affect query performance?
faq.answer: Compression usually improves query performance in analytical workloads because less data needs to be read from storage. The CPU cost of decompression is typically small compared to the I/O savings. Modern columnar engines are optimized for this tradeoff.
